plan.notes: Transcribed 2026-11-16 by live browser from Bakersfield College's official Program Pathways Mapper (https://programmap.bakersfieldcollege.edu/, reached from the college's official program-mapper page; no login required or attempted). The map is headed 'Law, Public Policy, and Society map for 2026-2027' and the pathway is for catalog year 2026-2027. Source map URL is this plan's source_url. Card View and Table View agreed exactly on every fixed course, category, unit value and term total; the printed wording of choice-slot headings differs between the views on this map, so slot titles below use the Card View wording and each slot's note also gives its Table View wording. The inventoried program 'Law, Public Policy, and Society' is listed in the mapper under that name; the program details state the student will be awarded an Associate in Arts for Transfer (AA-T) degree and that 'This degree requires a total of 60 units.' This plan transcribes the first-listed 2026-2027 pathway, 'Bakersfield College / Law, Public Policy, and Society / Associate in Arts for Transfer / 61-65.5 units / 4 terms / to CSU Bakersfield', in full; the page shows only the 4-term Bakersfield College segment. DISCREPANCY DISCLOSED: the 2026-2027 program page lists this pathway as '60-68 units', but the pathway page reached by its own link is headed 61-65.5 units and its term totals sum to 61-65.5; this transcription follows the pathway page itself. The second 2026-2027 pathway continues to a CSU Bakersfield Public Administration BA (60 units, Terms 5-8); its Bakersfield College segment (Terms 1-4) is identical to the pathway transcribed here, and the CSU segment is a different institution's degree, so it is not collected as a separate plan. In 2025-2026 a detailed map with the same structure existed. The transcribed map prints term totals as 15 / 15-17.5 / 16-18 / 15. Ranged rows: Term 2 'Area 1B : Critical Thinking and Composition' (3-4) and 'Quantitative Reasoning' (3-4.5); Term 3 'Area 5A : Physical Sciences' (3-5). Per the standing minimum-credit convention every ranged row is recorded at its printed minimum, so every term sum equals the map's printed term total at its minimum and the plan total is the printed minimum of 61 units. COMM C1000, ENGL C1000, PHIL B10 and POLS C1000 are printed with the dual category label 'Major / Gen Ed'; they are named major courses and are recorded with category 'major'. The 'Quantitative Reasoning' and 'US History' slots are likewise printed 'Major / Gen Ed' and are recorded with category 'major'. Card View heads two slots in each of Terms 3 and 4 identically as 'Major List A'; Table View distinguishes them as 'CalGETC Area 4, List A' and 'CalGETC Area 4, List B' - they are recorded here with distinct slot codes (BC-LISTA / BC-LISTB) and each slot's note gives both wordings. PHIL B8 (Term 2) is the only row on the map with a 'Prerequisites' flag in Card View; no other row shows a 'Prerequisites', 'Corequisites' or 'Dual Enrollment' flag, so no other prereqs are recorded. General-education, major-list and elective slots are transcribed exactly as printed as unselected 'Choose a course from ...' choice slots; the option lists behind those slots are not enumerated. Milestone rows printed on the map carry no course content and are not encoded. No separate Certificate program named Law, Public Policy, and Society exists in the mapper. The map page states verbatim: 'Program maps are for reference only. Make an appointment to create a customized education plan or visit CSU Transfer Planner for more options.'
